self_assessment: Implemented a focused rewrite of incdec_number (plus two small helpers) covering every requirement bullet -- percent-encoded-triplet masking, port never modified, default segments={'path'}, ValueError for bad op/count, IncDecError for no-match and decrement-count-exceeds-value, zero-padding preserve/widen/no-add, and FullyEncoded+TolerantMode get/set so encoded data round-trips byte-exact; verified with 176 standalone assertions (36 requirement-focused + 140 replicating the base commit's own test_urlutils.py::TestIncDecNumber cases, since the pinned old pytest doesn't collect under the installed pytest 9.1.1) -- all pass, with two knowingly reinterpreted spots I couldn't fully resolve from spec text alone: (1) segment search priority was implemented as reverse-URL-order (anchor, query, path, host) rather than the literal 'path, query, anchor, host' phrasing in the last requirement bullet, because reverse order is what the base commit's own test_incdec_segment_ignored asserts and matches the 'last numeric sequence' framing; (2) 'port' was dropped entirely from the valid override segments (any segments request including it now raises IncDecError) per 'Port numbers must never be modified' and the explicit override subset {host,path,query,anchor}, which intentionally breaks the base commit's old test_incdec_port/test_incdec_port_default (which exercised the old, presumably-removed port-modifying behavior).
